extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of online journalism (journalism students, instructors, early-career reporters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for producing news stories specifically for the web, covering mechanics, style, multimedia integration, and ethical/legal issues. Emphasizes practical techniques, examples, style tests, and exercises to build mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Students learn the basic mechanics ... of online newswriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers foundational mechanics for writing news for the web; material delivered via explanatory/descriptive text, examples, models, and simulated news copy to build practical skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow (how a story moves and is organized) is taught as a core element of online newswriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes coherent organization and logical progression appropriate to online readers; practiced through exercises and simulated news copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Style: the appropriate voice and word choices for online news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes style tests to assess mastery; guidance aims to blend the best of traditional news writing with web-specific conventions (concise, scannable, clear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone: the overall attitude and register suited to online audiences and the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses choosing a tone that fits mass-consumption web news while maintaining journalistic standards; examples and models illustrate appropriate tonal choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and techniques for producing online news — practical procedures and craft skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaches newsroom and web-appropriate methods (e.g., how to structure leads, update stories, use hyperlinks) using numerous examples, models, and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictures, graphics, audio and video (multimedia integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write online news stories incorporating pictures, graphics, audio and video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on integrating multimedia with text effectively for the web; examples and models show best practices for combining media elements with copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making good online newswriting better
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies and techniques aimed at improving already competent online newswriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced tips and refinements for stronger web journalism practice; likely includes editing, optimization for readability, and enhancement of storytelling with multimedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and ethical concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of legal and ethical issues/concerns relevant to online journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses ethical considerations and legal constraints (e.g., libel, privacy, attribution) tailored to web publishing; intended to inform responsible reporting and publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style tests and writing exercises (assessment of mastery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Style tests let users easily assess how well they are mastering concepts and skills; includes writing exercises and simulated news copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical tools (style tests, exercises, simulated assignments) are used both to teach and to evaluate proficiency in online newswriting techniques and stylistic conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend of mass-consumption writing and web best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes how to blend the best of writing news for mass consumption with web-specific practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance focuses on adapting traditional news values (clarity, accuracy, accessibility) to the web, ensuring stories serve broad online audiences while leveraging web affordances (links, multimedia, updates).
